LESSON: BUILDINGS IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Our Neighbourhood
Topic 4.2: Buildings in the Neighbourhood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Buildings in the Neighbourhood, part of Our Neighbourhood in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have buildings in the neighbourhood?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Buildings in the Neighbourhood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
⚫ Citizenship: learner develops sense of belonging when identifying the buildings in the neighbourhood and their uses.

Values:
• Patriotism: learner enhances citizenship when appreciating buildings in the neighbourhood.

• Unity: learner teams up with peers to construct simple structures of buildings found in the neighbourhood.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
⚫ Financial literacy: learner practices buying and selling in the shop corner.

Link to other learning area:

⚫ Buildings found in the neighbourhood relates to places of worship in Religious Activities..

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips, charts, name cards, and pictures and picture cut outs about buildings in the neighbourhood, theme-based multi- purpose Communication Board, adapted digital devices, songs and poems about buildings in the neighbourhood, universal cuffs

with padded pencils, crayons with grips, slant boards, foot-boards for learners using lower extremities, book holders and page

turners, positioning/ seating devices whose worktops/ table tops are at a suitable height, mobility devices such as wheelchairs/

crutches, head/ mouth pointers, splints for hands/ hand stabilizers, adapted tools such as light hammers and saws with padded

handles, holy books (Bible.....or their imitation)

Related Service Providers: Physiotherapist, Occupational Therapist, Learner Support Assistant/ Scribe
